topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and presents the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin, RTK/Ras/MAPK, and PI3K/Akt pathways, drive uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in leukemias and solid tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells arrest normal lineage maturation to maintain proliferative states across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death by disrupting p53 signaling and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere biology, replicative immortality, and cell-autonomous growth summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms of replicative senescence and telomerase reactivation that confer cellular immortality, the convergence of stress signaling on p53, and summarize cell-autonomous growth control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism, aerobic glycolysis, and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells through aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific rewiring, and Krebs cycle mutations generating oncogenic metabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and regulatory balance required to establish new vasculature for supplying oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metastatic cascade, the clinical utility of circulating tumor cells, the seed-and-soil dynamics, and the genomic characteristics associated with metastatic progression.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the synthesis of cancer hallmarks and inviting student follow-up.
